summary: A walled compound featuring two tall watchtowers and a central building with a zigzagging footprint. The structure is characterized by its distinctively striped walls made of alternating bands of stone brick, wood, white blocks, and brick, along with flat, dark roofs.

shape.overall_form: Rectangular walled enclosure with a Z-shaped central structure and two corner towers

materials.name: stonebrick
materials.role: wall stripes, tower corners, roof edging

materials.name: quartz_block
materials.role: wall stripes, vertical pillars, ground perimeter outline

rebuild_hints: Begin by laying out the rectangular footprint and the Z-shaped central building.
Construct the walls using a repeating horizontal stripe pattern: stone brick, wood, white block, brick, and stone brick.
Integrate vertical white pillars along the walls to break up the horizontal bands.
Build the two tall brick towers at opposite corners, detailing them with stone brick corners and small windows.
Cap the towers and the main building with flat nether brick roofs, bordered by stone brick slabs.
Place a dotted outline of white blocks on the ground surrounding the entire complex.
uncertainties: The exact material of the white blocks (could be quartz, white concrete, or iron).
The interior layout and whether the main building has multiple internal levels.
The exact block count for the dimensions.
